items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: two good tenor players, Don Bias and Dick Wilson

ctx.x: One block down. It was in the old Cotton Club building. The Golden Gate Ballroom. Sometimes on a weekend, there would be five bands in there. But my big band, and Andy Kirk -- we were the house bands, and Andy Kirk had a wonderful band there, too. He had Mary Lou Williams on piano, and Don Byas was his featured tenor. He had

two good tenor players, Don Bias and Dick Wilson -- and he had one of my favorite lead trumpet players, Big Jim -- and I don't know Big Jim's last name, but he was one of the great trumpet players of all time.

Yeah. Jim ... I know his name because he works for the subway now, if he hasn't passed away, because my wife was a friend of his wife's. And they also had a John Williams, MaryLou Williams' husband, who was a baritone sax player.
